note: Adjudicated acceptance outcomes. A group listed here has been investigated and its gap attributed with evidence; check_acceptance.py reports it as explained instead of failing forever. Adding an entry requires evidence in docs/investigations.md — not a hunch.

tfn_mosi.attribution: MMSA's own code does not reach MMSA's own published Corr. Run on identical data, seeds 42-46 and device, it scores 0.6456 +- 0.0136 against the table's 0.6733 — short by 0.0277, twice our 0.0138, with none of its five seeds reaching the target. Ours scores 0.6595 on the same footing: better than the reference implementation. Device is not the explanation — our code moves 0.0007 between CUDA and CPU.
tfn_mosi.do_not_retry: Re-auditing the port. Nine hypotheses were ruled out and three implementations agree line by line; the shortfall is in the target, not the code. If it is revisited, the open questions are the device (MMSA's table was most likely CUDA, this comparison is CPU) and its unstated seed set, not our implementation.
tfn_mosi.caveats: Five seeds rather than ten; CPU. The claim is that the published Corr is not reachable from MMSA's code under conditions we can control, NOT that it is wrong.
tfn_mosi.does_not_generalise: Established for TFN only. Any similar attribution for another group requires running MMSA for that group first.

ef_lstm_mosi.attribution: MMSA's own EF-LSTM collapses too — 1 seed in 10 against our 2, the same distribution at the ~23% rate measured over 30 seeds — so the instability belongs to the configuration, not the port. Neither implementation reaches the published figures: against Corr 0.6690 its code averages 0.6358 (highest seed 0.6558) and ours 0.6215 on seeds 42-46; against MAE 0.9488 its code averages 1.0236 and ours 1.0712. On non-collapsed seeds only, ours scores Corr 0.6485 against its 0.6424. **Ours is worse than its code on this subset** (MAE 1.0712 vs 1.0236, Corr 0.6215 vs 0.6358) and that is entirely the collapse count: we collapsed on seeds 46 and 48, it collapsed on 45. One collapse dominates a five-seed mean. The published MAE of 0.9488 would require no collapses at all.
ef_lstm_mosi.do_not_retry: Auditing the port for the collapse. It is a property of four LSTM layers with 0.5 inter-layer dropout on 1284 training samples, present in both implementations, measured at 23% over 30 seeds. What remains open is the criterion's blindness to a large absolute gap hidden by wide spread — a robustness dimension, not an implementation fix.
ef_lstm_mosi.caveats: CPU while MMSA's table was most likely CUDA; its table's seed set is unstated. The claim is that the published numbers are not reachable from MMSA's code under conditions we can control, NOT that they are wrong.
ef_lstm_mosi.does_not_generalise: Established for EF-LSTM and TFN only. The other nine groups each need their own MMSA run before any similar attribution.
ef_lstm_mosi.note_2026_07_31: MAE joined corr as a failure when the sigma cap landed: the criterion no longer lets two collapsed seeds inflate sigma to 0.2095 and turn a 3.2-noise-floor shortfall into +1.9 SE. That is the cap doing its job. The attribution is unchanged — the gap is the collapse rate, which both implementations share.
ef_lstm_mosi.note_2026_07_31_config_generation: The attribution now has a mechanism. MMSA's results table was written on 2021-05-06, when its EF-LSTM/MOSI config specified 2 LSTM layers, hidden 256, dropout 0.3, batch 128; today's specifies 4 layers, hidden 128, dropout 0.5, batch 32. Run at the 2021 config, ten seeds: MAE 0.9658 +- 0.0371 against the table's 0.9488, Corr 0.6510 against 0.6690, Acc-2 0.7800 against 0.7848, and ZERO collapsed seeds. The line above — 'the published MAE would require no collapses at all' — turns out to describe the configuration the table was actually written under. So the gap is largely a configuration-generation mismatch between subject and reference, not an implementation defect, and the 23% collapse rate belongs specifically to the four-layer stack. The acceptance group stays on today's config: switching to a better-scoring one after seeing the scores is forbidden. Evidence: docs/investigations.md#table-predates-config, group ef_lstm_mosi_2021config.

tfn_mosi (2026-07-26).was: Acc-2/Corr gap attributed to MMSA selecting hyper-parameters on the test set.
tfn_mosi (2026-07-26).retracted_because: The gap was ours. The acceptance run had been using our masked, length-aware pooling instead of MMSA's padding behaviour, which confounded reproduction fidelity with a change of our own. With the faithful port, TFN reproduces: MAE +0.5 SE, Acc-2 +1.0 SE. The test-selection observation about MMSA remains factually true and is still recorded in investigations.md, but it does not explain this gap and must not be cited as if it did.
tfn_mosi (2026-07-26).lesson: An adjudication is a claim about cause. Before recording one, rule out our own deviations from the reference — they are the most likely explanation and the cheapest to test.
